# Migrate from Hoppscotch

Everything below is what TestPion's Hoppscotch importer does today. An import never drops something silently: the Import dialog previews what will be created, and the compatibility report lists every item that came over with changes or not at all. See [Import fidelity](/getting-started/import-fidelity) for how the report reads.

## Export from Hoppscotch

1. **Collections ▸ ⋯ ▸ Export** (a JSON file).
2. **Environments ▸ ⋯ ▸ Export**.

## Import into TestPion

The files (drop them on the window or **Import** ▸ choose).

TestPion reads, by content (never by the file name):

- Collection exports (JSON; REST and GraphQL collections)
- Environment exports

On the command line: `testpion import <file|folder|zip|link> -w <workspace>` (several files, a folder or a ZIP are previewed first; `--apply` imports them). **Home ▸ Migrate from…** opens the same dialog with these steps.

## What comes over

- Folders and requests, params, headers, bodies by content type, request variables
- Collection and folder headers, variables and scripts
- Auth: basic, bearer, digest, API key, OAuth 2 (client credentials, password, authorization code), JWT
- Saved responses (examples), GraphQL requests
- Environments, with the secret flag (secret values to enter)

## What is changed on the way

- `pw.*` and `hopp.*` scripts become `tp.*`; Jest-style matchers (`toBe`, `toBeLevel2xx`, `toHaveLength` …) become chai (`to.equal`, `to.be.within(200, 299)` …); the `pm.*` layer of Hoppscotch scripts becomes `tp.*`
- `<<name>>` becomes `{{name}}`
- Request variables become lines that set them before the request

## What does not come over

- Auth schemes TestPion has not (AWS signature, Hawk, Akamai): No auth and a placeholder header
- `hopp.fetch`, `hopp.cookies` (marked `TODO(import)`)
- The OAuth 2 implicit grant

## Scripts (`pw.*`, `hopp.*`)

Scripts become TestPion's `tp.*`; anything the table does not list is left as written and still runs where the sandbox can run it.

| In the script | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `pw.test(…)` | `tp.test(…)` |
| `pw.expect` | `tp.expect` |
| `pw.env.get(a)` | `tp.environment.get(a)` |
| `pw.env.getResolve(a)` | `tp.variables.replaceIn('{{' + a + '}}')` |
| `pw.env.resolve(a)` | `tp.variables.replaceIn(a)` |
| `pw.env.set(a, b)` | `tp.environment.set(a, b)` |
| `pw.env.unset(a)` | `tp.environment.unset(a)` |
| `pw.response.status` | `tp.response.code` |
| `pw.response.body` | `tp.response.json()` |
| `pw.response.headers` | `tp.response.headers.all()` |
| `pw.response.responseTime` | `tp.response.responseTime` |
| `hopp.test(…)` | `tp.test(…)` |
| `hopp.expect` | `tp.expect` |
| `hopp.env.get(a)` | `tp.environment.get(a)` |
| `hopp.env.set(a, b)` | `tp.environment.set(a, b)` |
| `hopp.env.unset(a)` | `tp.environment.unset(a)` |
| `hopp.env.active.get(a)` | `tp.environment.get(a)` |
| `hopp.env.active.set(a, b)` | `tp.environment.set(a, b)` |
| `hopp.env.active.unset(a)` | `tp.environment.unset(a)` |
| `hopp.env.global.get(a)` | `tp.globals.get(a)` |
| `hopp.env.global.set(a, b)` | `tp.globals.set(a, b)` |
| `hopp.env.global.unset(a)` | `tp.globals.unset(a)` |
| `hopp.response.statusCode` | `tp.response.code` |
| `hopp.response.statusText` | `tp.response.status` |
| `hopp.response.responseTime` | `tp.response.responseTime` |
| `hopp.response.asJSON()` | `tp.response.json()` |
| `hopp.response.asText()` | `tp.response.text()` |
| `hopp.response.headers` | `tp.response.headers.all()` |
| `hopp.request.url` | `tp.request.url.toString()` |
| `hopp.request.method` | `tp.request.method` |
| `hopp.request.headers` | `tp.request.headers.all()` |
| `hopp.fetch` | no equivalent: a `TODO(import)` line and a finding |
| `hopp.cookies` | no equivalent: a `TODO(import)` line and a finding |
| `pm.*` | `tp.*` (Hoppscotch's Postman layer) |

Jest-style matchers after `pw.expect(x)` / `hopp.expect(x)` become chai:

| Matcher | Becomes |
|---|---|
| .toBe(…) | `.to.equal(…)` |
| .toEqual(…) | `.to.eql(…)` |
| .toBeLevel2xx(…) | `.to.be.within(200, 299)` |
| .toBeLevel3xx(…) | `.to.be.within(300, 399)` |
| .toBeLevel4xx(…) | `.to.be.within(400, 499)` |
| .toBeLevel5xx(…) | `.to.be.within(500, 599)` |
| .toBeType(…) | `.to.be.a(…)` |
| .toHaveLength(…) | `.to.have.lengthOf(…)` |
| .toInclude(…) | `.to.include(…)` |
| .toContain(…) | `.to.include(…)` |
| .toMatch(…) | `.to.match(…)` |
| .toHaveProperty(…) | `.to.have.property(…)` |
| .toBeTruthy(…) | `.to.be.ok(…)` |
| .toBeFalsy(…) | `.to.not.be.ok(…)` |
| .toBeNull(…) | `.to.be.null(…)` |
| .toBeUndefined(…) | `.to.be.undefined(…)` |
| .toBeGreaterThan(…) | `.to.be.above(…)` |
| .toBeLessThan(…) | `.to.be.below(…)` |
| .toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(…) | `.to.be.at.least(…)` |
| .toBeLessThanOrEqual(…) | `.to.be.at.most(…)` |

## Variables and templates

`<<name>>` and `<<$guid>>` become `{{name}}` and `{{$guid}}`.

## Importing again and going back

Import the same source again and TestPion **updates** the collection it made instead of adding a copy, matching on the `_ref_id` of each request and folder when the export has one, else the item path: the preview shows *replace*, *new* or *skip* for each item (an item you edited here is skipped unless you choose *replace*), and the update is one undo step.

:::
